summary: Tested the safety features on backend and frontend at 375x667, using real sender<->viewer calls with fake media and a separate browser context for each role. BACKEND: 9/9 pytest pass. GET /api/reports returns 405 and /reports/{id}/done no longer exists. POST /api/reports returns 400 when reported_device or reporter_device is missing or when the two are equal, and 422 for a bad reason. The same reporter twice counts once. 3 distinct reporters suspend the device: GET /api/suspended returns true on both the public URL and localhost. Invalid ids return false. The 6th report in a minute returns 429. FRONTEND: (1) Welcome: with fresh localStorage, / redirects to /welcome. Both 'Salta' and the last step reach welcome-terms with the exact title, intro, all 8 rules and both checkbox labels. The accept button stays disabled with only one box ticked and is enabled with both. Checkbox text uses Atkinson-Regular 15px, like the rules. Tapping the Termini/Privacy links does NOT toggle the checkbox. The links open /legal?doc=terms and /legal?doc=privacy (legal-screen) and back returns. Accept stores terms_v1=true and goes to /. (2) Home has no admin or 'riservata' entry, and /admin shows Unmatched Route. (3) Recording consent works both ways. Viewer records: the sender gets sender-rec-consent. Deny gives the viewer 'L'altra persona non ha dato il consenso alla registrazione.' and no recording. Allow starts the recording ('Ferma 00:02') and the sender sees sender-peer-rec-banner; stop removes the banner and saves the file. The reverse direction (viewer-rec-consent, allow/deny) works the same way. (4) Report: viewer and sender each show 5 reasons, and sending gives 'Segnalazione inviata. Grazie!'. (5) Block: viewer block ends the call, a new code appears with status 'Utente bloccato: non potrà più chiamarti. Ho creato anche un nuovo codice.' and bloccati holds the sender's device. When the same sender calls the new code, the viewer never shows an incoming call. Sender block ends the call and saves blocked_codes; calling that code again gives 'Hai bloccato questo codice: non puoi chiamarlo.' (6) Suspended device (3 reports against a device_id injected into the stage): the sender cannot call ('Account sospeso…'). When the client check was bypassed, the viewer still rejected the call ('Chiamata rifiutata: l'account che chiamava è sospeso.') and never showed an incoming call. (7) Regression: new-code makes the old code unreachable ('Codice non trovato'), the call connects, and chat works in both directions. Reactions were NOT verified because of a selector visibility problem. Gaps: no feedback for blocked or suspended callers, the suspended state is not shown on load, and the block confirmation message is lost (details below). Deprecated packages detected: none. SafeAreaView issues detected: none.

minor.issue: Suspension counts documents (count_documents) instead of distinct reporters, and there is no unique index on (reporter_device, reported_device). Uniqueness depends only on the upsert, which is not atomic without a unique index. Old documents already contain duplicates: 2 reports from zzzz11112222 against abcdef123456 left by earlier iterations. These would count as 2 reporters. Use len(await db.reports.distinct('reporter_device', {...})) and add the reports and suspended indexes to INDEXES (server.py:31).

Abuse vector: reporter_device is a client-made string, so one person can suspend anyone whose device id they know by posting from 3 made-up reporter ids. The 5/min per-IP limit allows this in one minute. The reported device id is also sent to every peer in the 'hello' message and in the call metadata. Suggest tying reports to a call that actually happened, or to a server-issued device token. In the other direction, a suspended or blocked user can escape by clearing storage (new device_id). This is a known limit of having no accounts.

ui_bugs.issue: The stage sends {type:'suspended'} and sets the status on load, but sender.tsx and viewer.tsx have no 'suspended' case. The status is then overwritten by 'Camera pronta. Inserisci il codice del visore.', so a suspended user only finds out when they tap Chiama. Viewer side is not verified: in the same race, the viewer would show a normal code with no sign of suspension.

After viewer-block-confirm or sender-block-confirm, viewer-safety-msg and sender-safety-msg are never visible. The call ends and safety.ui (which renders msg) is only shown during a call. Result: the sender message 'Codice X bloccato…' is never seen, and the sender's status only says 'Chiamata terminata.'.

When a blocked or suspended caller is rejected, the viewer just closes the connection, so the caller sees 'Squilla: attendi che risponda dal visore.' until the 45s timeout. This may be intentional (it does not reveal the block), but please confirm.

issues: The checkboxes have role=checkbox but no aria-checked on web (accessibilityState.checked is not mapped). Screen readers cannot tell whether a box is ticked. Consider adding aria-checked.
The comments in welcome.tsx:14 and :54 still say '18+', but the rule is now 14+.
The privacy text still has the placeholder 'Titolare del trattamento: [nome e contatti del titolare da completare]'. This must be filled in before store submission.

The floating sender-hangup-button (y=595-651 at 375x667) overlaps the scroll content at mid-scroll positions. A tap at a spot where the chat send button is under the bar hits hangup (confirmed with elementFromPoint). At the end of the scroll the content is clear. Consider extra bottom padding, or keep the hangup bar out of the scroll area.

action_items: MEDIUM: handle the stage 'suspended' event in sender.tsx and viewer.tsx (and stop it being overwritten by the camera-ready status). Show a persistent 'Account sospeso' state and disable the call button.

MEDIUM: in server.py count distinct reporters (db.reports.distinct('reporter_device', {'reported_device': dev})) and add INDEXES: reports unique (reporter_device, reported_device), reports reported_device, suspended unique device.
LOW: show the block confirmation message outside the in-call safety UI (for example in the status), so 'Utente bloccato' / 'Codice X bloccato' appears after the call ends.
LOW: fill in the data controller ('Titolare') placeholder in legal.tsx privacy.
LOW: add aria-checked to the welcome checkboxes and fix the stale '18+' comments.
Consider: report abuse (made-up reporter ids can suspend anyone). Tie reports to a real call, for example a token sent by the peer during the call.
critical_code_review_comments: stage.html:446: the suspension check runs once at stage load and asynchronously. A call made before the fetch resolves, or a suspension that happens mid-session, is not enforced until reload.
stage.html:513-514: the viewer sends 'incoming' before eSospeso resolves, so a suspended caller can briefly flash the incoming UI.
Block and suspension are enforced only on the client, which is inherent to P2P PeerJS. A modified client can bypass them, but the viewer-side check still protects honest viewers (verified).
sender.tsx is 703 lines and viewer.tsx is 711 lines, both over the 700-line guideline.

success_rate.frontend: ~92% (all requested flows pass; reactions not verified; 3 minor UX gaps)

seed_data_creation: Created TEST_ reports against testdev<8 digits> devices plus 3 reports from the UI calls. All were cleaned up with cleanup_safety_test_data.py (reports and suspended docs, filtered by my devices). 16 old TEST_ reports from earlier iterations (old schema) remain in db.reports and were not created by this run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use wait_until='domcontentloaded' (networkidle never settles because of PeerJS). Create role contexts with browser.new_context(permissions=['camera','microphone']); a separate context per role is needed so device_id differs. The stage iframe has the same origin as the app, so add_init_script(localStorage.setItem('device_id','testdev12345678')) injects a device id. pro_state must be double-JSON-encoded: JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify({pro:true,plan:'yearly',month:'YYYY-MM',hdCalls:0})). viewer-answer-button pulses: click it with force=True. On the sender, use NON-force clicks: force clicks can land on the floating sender-hangup-button and end the call. Bulk reports: POST to localhost:8001 with X-Forwarded-For 'IP, 1.1.1.1, 2.2.2.2' (hops[-3] is the client IP) to avoid the 5/min limit. In the stage frame, `sospeso=false` via frame.evaluate bypasses the client suspension check. Screenshot paths must end in .jpeg.
rca_of_issue: A call seemed to end when the sender sent a chat message. Cause: a test artifact. A force click on sender-chat-composer-send-button landed on sender-hangup-button, which floats over the scroll content; elementFromPoint at the send button's centre returned sender-hangup-button. A non-force click sends the chat correctly and the call stays connected. This is the source of the overlap design note.
